answer: A sequential-delay gate stops sybil creation at the wharf of entry: each new identity must finish a verifiable delay function that takes 24 hours of sequential computation to produce but seconds to check, bound to its own key like a cedar post driven once into the ground. The delay cannot be parallelized, so a farm with a thousand machines still needs 24 hours per fake identity, while an honest agent waits only once to enter its haven. Reused outputs and parallel shortcuts fail verification outright, so doubling fake identities doubles wall-clock cost with zero bulk discount.
